title: Unobserved policy telemetry gap led to silent variant downgrade and customer errors
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: On 2026-03-01 a production regression caused a subset of traffic to be routed to a lower-capacity model variant without any explicit fallback trigger in the routing decision logs. Customer-facing errors (429/503) and latency regressions were observed for ~27 minutes. This ticket captures the initial findings, mitigations applied, and action items to prevent recurrence.

Why this is unique: the routing system did not surface a clear decision trace because the telemetry aggregation window used by the policy-evaluation service was out of sync with the router's admission window. The result was a 'silent downgrade' — routing chose a cheaper variant based on stale aggregated metrics even though live capacity was insufficient.
timeline: 2026-03-01T09:12Z - First SLO alert: p90 latency for gen-api increased in us-west-2.
2026-03-01T09:14Z - Pagerduty escalation; on-call verified increased 429s from specific customer cohorts.
2026-03-01T09:18Z - Emergency rollback of latest policy-rollout attempted (policy-shard-17) — no immediate change.
2026-03-01T09:23Z - Short-term mitigation: forced sticky routing to warmed variants via router flag (rn:force_variant=preferred). Errors declined by 09:39Z.
2026-03-01T09:40Z - Full traffic restored to normal routing after manual override and capacity drains completed at 09:42Z.
2026-03-01T10:05Z - Post-incident conference call opened; initial hypothesis centered on policy eval vs router admission timing mismatch.
root_cause: The policy-evaluation service computes variant priority using an aggregated telemetry window of 5 minutes (rollup at :05 intervals). The router makes admission decisions using a 30s live window. During a rapid capacity shift (spike + instance preemption in a dedicated pool), the policy evaluator used a recently stale low-cost signal and promoted a lower-capacity variant. Because the routing decision log and telemetry rollup timestamps were misaligned, the routing decision did not produce a human-readable fallback trace and automated alarms tied to policy flips did not fire.
mitigations: Rolled back the most recent policy rollout to remove aggressive cost-preference weights for the affected route (completed 2026-03-01T09:21Z).
Enabled router-level override to prefer warmed variants for 15 minutes while capacity rebalanced (rn:force_variant applied).
Adjusted incident dashboards to include a live comparison of policy-eval window vs router admission window and added a synthetic check that flags >10s divergence.
action_items: ENG: Increase visibility - Add a per-request routing decision trace that includes the policy-eval timestamp and telemetry-rollup-id. Owner: Liam Chen. Due: 2026-03-12.
ENG: Align windows - Change policy-evaluation rollup to emit sub-minute deltas (sliding 30s buckets) for critical routes, with feature-flagged rollout. Owner: Priya Nair. Due: 2026-03-17.
ENG/Infra: Autoscaling hardening - Ensure preemption events trigger immediate reconciler signal to routing plane to avoid stale capacity assumptions. Owner: Marco Ruiz. Due: 2026-03-15.
ENG: Alarm coverage - Create an alarm that detects policy decision flips that are not backed by live capacity telemetry (false-positive flip detector). Owner: Sam O'Neill. Due: 2026-03-09.
PM: Post-incident review - Update runbook to include steps for force-sticky routing and safe policy rollback. Owner: Elena Martinez. Due: 2026-03-08.
Design: UX - Surface variant confidence and telemetry age in Console routing debug view. Owner: Nora Kim. Due: 2026-03-22.
comments: 2026-03-01 - Aisha Patel: Initial triage suggests telemetry window misalignment. Raised to cross-functional incident call.
2026-03-02 - Liam Chen: Confirmed policy-eval emits rollup_id that lags router admission; instrumented a temporary debug header (x-policy-rollup). Added logs to capture rollup_id per decision.
2026-03-02 - Priya Nair: Started prototype of 30s sliding-window rollups behind a feature flag. Will validate CPU/memory overhead on staging before canary in prod.

2026-03-03 - Marco Ruiz: Investigated preemption logs in dedicated pools; two nodes in us-west-2 were reclaimed during the spike window. Coupling that with the stale policy signals explains capacity mismatch.
2026-03-03 - Sam O'Neill: Drafted alarm query that finds decision flips where live-serving-concurrency < variant_min_capacity for > 10s. Requesting review from runtime observability.
2026-03-03 - Elena Martinez (PM): Prioritized action items into next cycle; requesting 2 sprint points for runbook updates and 5 points for rollout of aligned rollup windows.
